q: Write a detailed note on the industrial stage?
a: Answer. 1. Beginning of Industrial Stage: People started leading settled and organized life by now. The industrial stage began with the family economy. The family units produced their consumption goods like pots, tools, furniture, shoes, clothes, etc. With the increase in human needs, the handicraft system came into being. People adopted particular professions like a weaver, carpenter, goldsmith, porter, etc. In this way, the remarkable development in production, consumption, and exchange took place with the introduction of coins of gold and silver. The division of labor improved during this period. 2. Auxiliaries to Trade: The main blessings of this stage are: most modern machines, national and international marketing, developed communication and transport, modem currency and banking systems, telephone, radio, T.V, joint stock companies, stock exchange, etc. 3. Three Periods of Industrial Stage: Domestic system followed by handicraft and family Economy system gave birth to master-craftsmen, who opened small industries. They sold their production to the capitalists, who were responsible to sell those goods among the people. During this period monetary system was improved and government-issued currency and coins as legal tenders. Different types of machines in crude form were invented and a Banking system was also introduced. 4. Industrial Revolution: Modem industrial system is the successor of the domestic, cottage, and small-scale industry systems. It begins in the early eighteenth century when large-scale or mass production was needed. The factory system, the machine age, and the Industrial Revolution are different names for this system.

q: Define Capitalism and state its characteristics?
a: Answer. 1. Capitalism: Capitalism is a system, in which private individuals and companies are allowed to acquire the means of production and are given the liberty to use them or not to use them with a view to their own profit. 2. Characteristics of Capitalism: a. Private Property: Every individual is allowed to acquire the rights of private property. He is at liberty to use, consumes, manage, exchanges or inherit his property from others. b. freedom of Enterprise The individual can adopt any business he likes, provided it complies with the laws of the state. He can produce and sell. c. Freedom of Contract The individual is free to enter into any contract with his fellow citizens for his own profit. The government respects these contracts but interferes only when there is a danger of the exploitation of laborers. d. Price mechanism Price of goods are determined by the interaction of the forces of demand and supply. Equilibrium is restored to its actual position by the price mechanism. e. Profit Motive Capitalists invest their capital in occupations and industries where chances of greater profit exit. f. The sovereignty of the Consumer. A consumer is compared to a king. He has money that him, he can buy whatever commodity he likes. The industrialist are his humble servants. They are to produce goods strictly in accordance with the requirements of the consumers.

Explain its merits and demerits? Answer. 1. Socialism: Socialism is a program of reforms that refuses to accept the private ownership of the means of production and competitive control of industry. 2. Merits of Socialism: In this system, the factors of production are owned by the state and utilized by the Government for the welfare of the people. Production is not meant for profit motive. The liking and disliking of consumers have no importance. Private property, professions, businesses, and productions are not allowed. In short, the Government controls all kinds of production, commerce trade, and business, and individuals are not allowed to do so. Socialism reduces the inequality of income. They keep the prices of commodities at a reasonable level. Socialism fulfills the basic necessities of the people. Development of the economy takes place under a single economic plan. Every individual has the right to work, rest, and recreation. Entire national income is distributed in the interest of all the working people. There is no class conflict and no exploitation. Social equality prevails as all power belongs to the working people. 3. Demerits of Socialism: a. Consumer sovereignty is lost i.e. consumers are at the mercy of the state. They are slaves of the government. b. Control of the government, if corrupt people come in power, people suffer. c. It curbs individual incentive to work as necessaries of life are assured by the state.
